newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says investors interested in buying El Al.
newsitem.headline: Israel says investors interested in buying El Al.

text.p: Israel said domestic and foreign investors had shown interest in buying state-owned El Al Israel Airlines despite an estimated loss of $100 million in 1996, its first deficit in a decade.

The Transport Ministry said it had given its director-general, Nahum Lagenthal, head of a joint team with the Finance Ministry, 30 days to determine the manner of privatisation and present a detailed timetable.
A statement said the decision was taken "to accelerate the privatisation process of El Al".

"Lagenthal disclosed that groups of Israeli and foreign investors had in recent days asked the Transport Ministry about buying El Al. He stressed that in one of the companies a foreign company is a partner," the statement said.

A ministry spokesman could not be reached for comment on a report by the Israeli financial daily Globes that a foreign airline and another foreign company, apparently from Europe, were interested in buying the national carrier.
El Al spokesman Nachman Klieman said he knew nothing about the report, saying any decision about privatisation would have to come from the state itself.
El Al said in October that a decline in tourism caused by Middle East violence would cause an estimated loss of $100 million in 1996. The carrier had a net profit of $15 million in 1995.
Airline president Yoel Feldshuh said in October that although he supported privatisation, short-term prospects were not good because of the expected loss.
The ministry statement said the joint team would be asked to determine whether to first privatise El Al's sister companies or to privatise all of them at the same time.
